results.title: PNVF giving stakeholders stronger voice
results.description: Stakeholders will now have a direct and stronger voice in the formation of the national volleyball teams heading into major international tournaments. Philippine National Volleyball Federation (PNVF) Executive Director Atty. Miguel Carlos Pacifico F. Suarez announced on Friday, Oct. 16, that the federation is taking a highly-collaborative approach by creating a dedicated National Team Commission. The five-man panel is designed to enable major stakeholders to air their concerns and align schedules before formally assembling the rosters for the Alas Pilipinas Men and Women squads. Suarez emphasized that the creation of the commission ensures the federation leadership moves away from the old practice of making unilateral decisions regarding national team selection, calendar management, and player availability. No less than PNVF president Frank Lao will chair the powerful body with key stakeholders like Sherwin Malonzo of the Premier Volleyball League, Dr. Ian Laurel of the Shakey’s Super League, Fr. Victor Calvo of the National Collegiate Athletic Association and Bo Perasol of the University Athletic Association of the Philippines as members. Malonzo and Laurel bring deep administrative experience from previous PNVF setups, while Calvo and Perasol oversee the nation’s top collegiate sports programs, ensuring full representation across all levels of Philippine volleyball. “The establishment of the National Team Commission is a major step in the right direction. By giving stakeholders a direct and stronger voice, we are ensuring a more inclusive, transparent, and collaborative approach to forming and supporting our national team,” Suarez said in an official statement. “With this special panel, we are removing the old practice of leadership making unilateral decisions without consulting key stakeholders on player schedules and availability. We are now giving everyone a unified voice to guarantee a far more collaborative and sustainable national team program.” Since taking the helm of the PNVF last August, Lao has prioritized integrity, transparency, and accountability. To stabilize the organization, the businessman-sportsman used his personal funds to settle outstanding financial liabilities and obligations inherited from previous administrations. Among his first major technical reforms was revamping the coaching staff of both national squads—bringing back head coach Dante Alinsunurin to lead Alas Pilipinas Men, and tapping veteran Italian strategist Angiolino Frigoni to steer Alas Pilipinas Women. Alinsunurin previously led the male spikers to a historic silver-medal finish at the 30th Southeast Asian Games in 2019, while Frigoni brings world-class pedigree, having guided the Italian women's team to the 2000 Sydney Olympics and coached the Dutch women's national squad. “Our president, Mr. Frank Lao, is delivering on his commitment to drive genuine reforms within the federation,” Suarez added. “Giving the volleyball community a seat at the table is essential because we are expecting more changes to come as we move forward towards rebuilding the federation and leading it to greater heights.”

results.title: JAZA warns AI, climate risks threaten Philippine investments
results.description: Unchecked technological disruption, geopolitical fragmentation, and severe climate events are exposing structural vulnerabilities that risk undermining long-term investment in the Philippines, according to tycoon Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala. Speaking at the Makati Business Club’s 45th anniversary gala on Thursday evening, Zobel, who is the organization’s vice chairman, warned that the Philippines must urgently address critical gaps in its economy. Achieving sustained growth will require deeper business-to-business cooperation alongside enhanced public-private partnerships, Zobel said. Among the immediate headwinds is the rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), which threatens to disrupt key pillars of the domestic economy, particularly the business process outsourcing and knowledge-based services sectors that generate billions of pesos in foreign exchange earnings annually. “We are likewise all too familiar with the rapid disruption brought about by new technologies,” Zobel said. “AI is particularly significant for the Philippines, given the importance of business process and knowledge-based outsourcing to our economy.” Beyond technology, shifting geopolitical dynamics are actively rewriting global commerce. As nations prioritize national security and supply-chain resilience over pure cost efficiency, historical trade patterns are being upended. Trade flows that were once dictated strictly by value creation are now governed by strategic alliances and risk mitigation. Concurrently, severe weather events— from destructive typhoons to intense El Niño climate patterns—continue to test the resiliency of local infrastructure and threaten macroeconomic stability. While digital transformation, regional integration, and the transition toward clean energy offer immense upside for the Philippine economy, Zobel emphasized that these trends will only yield lasting benefits if they translate into higher productivity and quality job creation for the local workforce. To capitalize on these shifts, Zobel called on corporate leaders to establish unified action platforms and foster a candid dialogue with government regulators. “We need an honest conversation among ourselves and with our partners in the public sector about whether we have the talent, infrastructure, energy, regulatory environment, and institutional stability needed to attract long-term investment,” Zobel said. “I suspect many of us already have a good sense of where the gaps are. What we need are effective platforms to work through these together,” he added.

results.title: Tight available supply after contract rollover combined with recovering demand pushed spot premiums higher than yesterday [SMM Shanghai spot copper]
results.description: [SMM SHFE Copper Spot] Looking ahead to tomorrow, after SHFE copper completes the contract rollover, the spot market quotation benchmark will switch to the 2611 contract. Intraday futures staged a pullback, prompting some downstream copper processing enterprises to release orders and procurement demand. Combined with the relatively tight availability of circulating supply in the market, suppliers showed strong willingness to hold back from selling and hold prices firm, jointly driving spot premiums sharply higher. On the supply side, the delivery volume for the SHFE copper 2610 contract was 4,895 lots. After delivery is completed, close attention should be paid to the pace of warrant cancellations and the return of supply to the spot market. If delivered supply is released in a concentrated manner, the tightness of available supply in the Shanghai market may ease somewhat, and current high premiums will face some pullback pressure. However, if warrant outflows remain slow, the short-term tight supply pattern will continue to support premiums. On the demand side, attention should be paid to whether downstream new orders can sustain volume growth amid high copper prices. Overall, Shanghai spot premiums are expected to continue to consolidate at highs tomorrow, but the room for further sharp upside may be relatively limited.
